newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese bonds calm despite govt threat to quit.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese bonds calm despite govt threat to quit.

text.p: 1115 GMT - Portuguese government bonds were steady despite the government's threat to quit if parliament pushed through opposition proposals on local government spending. The Independence Day holiday in the U.S. also weighed on liquidity. *Sept 97 futures up 0.02 points to 110.77 *Feb 07 cash (OTC) 102.22 (102.20), yld 6.31 (6.31) *Spread vs 10-yr cash Bund 72 bps vs 72 bps

Portuguese bonds were steady in early trade and dealers said they would remain in a tight range as investors ignored a threat by the government to quit if the parliament pushed through opposition spending proposals.
"The market opened calm, without volatility, and was not concerned by the Prime Minister's threat to resign," said one operator.
Analysts said Portugal remained on track to qualify to join the European single currency from the start.

"The spread against Bunds could narrow to 68 or 69 basis points, but the level will depend on Bunds, our guiding force today. Liquidity will be limited in the local market because of the holiday in the U.S.," a fixed income analyst said.
